title: Five Senses Sit Spot
description: Pause somewhere safe and notice the living details around you without rushing.
tasks: Read this mission, then put your phone away.
Sit safely for two quiet minutes.
Notice one sound, texture, scent, color, and movement.
Leave every plant and animal undisturbed.
observation_tips: Look slowly from left to right.
Never touch an unknown plant or animal.
reflection_question: What did you notice only after becoming still?

title: Bird Behavior Walk
description: Practice identifying birds by behavior and habitat rather than guessing from a single glimpse.
tasks: Walk slowly along an edge habitat.
Count birds without approaching nests.
Note size, color blocks, movement, and call direction.
Compare how birds use trees, ground, or open space.
observation_tips: Use binoculars if you have them; keep a respectful distance.
Do not play calls or feed wildlife.
reflection_question: Which behavior gave you the strongest clue?

title: Leaf Detective
description: Explore plant diversity by comparing leaves without picking them.
tasks: Find three different living plants.
Compare leaf shape, arrangement, edges, and texture visually.
Sketch or photograph one leaf in place.
Check the underside only if it is already accessible.
observation_tips: Avoid touching sap and wash hands after exploring.
Do not taste or collect unknown plants.
reflection_question: How did the plants differ even in the same area?

title: Microhabitat Survey
description: Map a tiny patch of ground and observe the relationships within it.
tasks: Choose a path edge or garden patch.
Observe insects, moisture, shade, and plant cover.
Record three interactions you see from a distance.
Restore your viewpoint without moving rocks or logs.
observation_tips: Never handle insects, nests, or decomposing material.
reflection_question: What made this small habitat suitable for life?

title: Tree Time Capsule
description: Read one tree through its structure, neighbors, and signs of seasonal change.
tasks: Choose a tree without climbing it.
Observe bark, canopy shape, and fallen leaves.
Look for signs of birds or insects without disturbing them.
Compare the tree with two nearby species.
observation_tips: Stay out from under unstable branches.
Do not carve, peel, or shake the tree.
reflection_question: What story does the tree's structure suggest?

title: Seasonal Field Notes
description: Create a careful, repeatable observation route for a longer outing.
tasks: Walk a safe loop and choose three observation points.
Spend five minutes at each point.
Record weather, species clues, sounds, and changes in light.
Plan one question to revisit next week.
observation_tips: Tell someone your route and carry water.
Follow local trail and wildlife rules.
reflection_question: What would become visible if you repeated this route?

title: Nature Photo Story
description: Make a small visual story about patterns, not close-up wildlife portraits.
tasks: Choose a safe, public location.
Capture three wide or context-rich images.
Look for repetition, contrast, and signs of seasonal change.
Keep your distance and avoid disturbing subjects.
observation_tips: Never use flash near wildlife or nests.
Leave no trace and respect private property.
reflection_question: What pattern connects your three images?
